name: Cape Cod National Seashore
blurb: Dunes, pine barrens and cold seas where seals draw in great white sharks.

tip.title: Remove the gray seals
tip.text: Seals eat sand lance and feed sharks and coyotes. Set Gray seal to -100% and watch the great white shark, the coyote and the gulls that scavenge them.

sources.title: NPS: Nature and science at Cape Cod National Seashore

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Drives growth of the dune plants, pines and the plankton of the bay and open ocean.

nodes.name: Cold Gulf of Maine water
nodes.desc: Cool, nutrient-bearing water around the outer Cape feeds plankton, which supports fish, seals and whales.

nodes.name: Shifting sand dunes
nodes.desc: Wind and waves keep the sandy shore moving; only plants adapted to salt spray and drifting sand can hold it.

nodes.name: Bacteria and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, shellfish and carcasses, returning nutrients to the sandy soil.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Microscopic algae that form the base of the marine food web off the Cape.

nodes.name: American beachgrass
nodes.desc: A dune grass whose spreading roots and stems trap blowing sand and help build and hold dunes.

nodes.name: Pitch pine
nodes.desc: A hardy pine of sandy, poor soils that dominates much of the Cape's pine barrens woodland.

nodes.name: Black cherry
nodes.desc: A common native tree and shrub of the Cape whose leaves and fruit are food for deer and small mammals.

nodes.name: Copepods
nodes.desc: Tiny planktonic crustaceans that graze on phytoplankton and feed small fish.

nodes.name: Blue mussel
nodes.desc: A filter-feeding mussel of rocky and sandy shores that strains plankton from the water.

nodes.name: American sand lance
nodes.desc: A small schooling fish that eats plankton and is a key prey of seals, whales and seabirds.

nodes.name: White-tailed deer
nodes.desc: Browses woody plants and fruit across the Cape's woods and heaths.

nodes.name: Meadow vole
nodes.desc: A small grassland rodent that eats plants and seeds and is prey for foxes and coyotes.

nodes.name: American red squirrel
nodes.desc: Eats conifer seeds and other plant foods; a common resident of the pine woods.

nodes.name: Common eider
nodes.desc: A sea duck that dives for mussels and other shellfish along the coast.

nodes.name: Humpback whale
nodes.desc: A baleen whale that feeds in nearby waters on schooling fish such as sand lance.

nodes.name: Gray seal
nodes.desc: Hunts fish, especially sand eels, and hauls out in large numbers on outer Cape beaches.

nodes.name: Great black-backed gull
nodes.desc: A large gull that eats shellfish and fish and scavenges carrion, including seal remains.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: Preys on rodents, squirrels and birds, and also eats fruit.

nodes.name: Great white shark
nodes.desc: Drawn to the Cape's seal colonies, where it hunts gray seals near shore.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: The Cape's top land predator; eats deer, small mammals and carrion.
